message.subject: Re: Stage37 guard applied; narrow final check
message.body:
Narrow check done on 550e1fa, alias_observation.go only, read-only in your worktree. No build, no tests, no broader review. The requested hardening and comment are both present and correct as described. Nothing blocking.

WHAT I VERIFIED, four points.

1. Guard. The condition now reads ctx != nil and namesOnly and scope != nil and scope.Policy != nil and scope.Allowed(dir, true) and discoveryWalkCacheFrom(ctx) != nil. That is the parity with vue.go I asked for: the directory is now classified under the live policy before any listing is handed back. It is behavior-preserving on refusal, because a refused directory falls through to overlayReadDir, which calls Scope.ReadDir, which applies the same predicate and returns fs.ErrNotExist exactly as it did before the change. So the guard removes a class of cross-policy reuse without introducing a new error path.

One placement observation, not a defect and not a change request. Allowed is evaluated before discoveryWalkCacheFrom, so it now runs on every namesOnly call even in builds with no walk cache and no probe, where reuse could never engage. Policy.Classify is side-effect-free so this is correctness-neutral; it is a small unconditional classify on a path that previously did a cheap nil check first. If you want the check confined to reuse-eligible calls, swapping the last two conjuncts gives identical semantics. Given the frozen-SHA rule I am explicitly not asking for that before timing.

2. One-policy-per-probe invariant. Stated at lines 16-17: the probe and cache are created together under one immutable policy in newDiscovery and must not be shared across policies. I confirmed the factual half of that sentence at 550e1fa: discovery.go:83 installs both in a single expression inside (*TSExtractor).newDiscovery at discovery.go:80, next to scope := e.inputScope at line 81, and that is the only non-test site that installs a probe. session.go:1385 installs a walk cache with no probe, so probeFrom returns nil there and reuse cannot engage, which is consistent with the comment rather than an exception to it.

Scope limit on what the guard buys, so the archive does not overread it. Allowed(dir, true) classifies the directory being read; it does not attest to the policy under which the child names in that recorded set were filtered. If a second probe site ever appeared under a broader policy, a reused listing could still be a subset filtered by the narrower one, and the directory check would pass. The invariant in the comment is what closes that, and it is now written down where a future second call site will see it. That is exactly the division I intended, so I consider risk 1 addressed.

3. Completed-listing map membership. Line 26, inside the critical section: map membership means complete, recordDir never stores partial listings. That is the right framing and it sits at the one line where the two-value map index is easy to misread as a computed flag. It matches the recordDir contract in overlay.go and the observe.go behavior that records nothing for a failed listing and deletes on SkipDir or walk error.

4. First-enumeration semantics. Lines 17-20 now say that within one build aliases use the first completed enumeration, including when the live directory later changes or becomes unreadable, and that this reduces independent observations without itself proving filesystem inputs stayed stable during a run. That covers both remaining risks from my earlier review: the within-run mutation shift, and the unreadable-directory case where reuse returns a nil error and therefore does not take the aliasesAtDir fallback or stop recursion. Both are now documented as intended behavior rather than latent. The earlier cross-run reobservation-fence sentence at lines 14-15 is retained and the new text supplements it rather than replacing it, which is the shape I suggested. The last clause is the part I most wanted, because it keeps the comment from being quotable later as a stability proof.

LOCKING SHAPE unchanged, checked line by line against fca10d8. The diff inside the critical section is a comment only. There is still exactly one unconditional probe.mu.Unlock() before any return, the entries slice is built entirely under the lock, the sort and return happen after it, and overlayReadDir is never called while the lock is held. aliasObservedEntry is untouched: Name, IsDir, Type and Info are byte-identical to the version I reviewed, so Info returning fs.ErrInvalid remains unreachable on the namesOnly path.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, per your scope. I did not read or review the new test cases, so I am not confirming the stale new directory, live control, reobservation refusal, removed-empty directory, callback live error or policy refusal tests beyond noting that alias_observation_test.go grew by 73 lines in this commit and that the four cases you named are the four gaps I had flagged. I did not re-review the ts.go call site, the mechanism, or the harness files that also landed in 550e1fa. No build, no test run, no timing.

I remain idle and source-only through the 17:10-17:55 UTC window and will not launch anything during the timing arms. Two offers from my earlier message still stand whenever you want them, neither urgent: pinning the digests of the Stage37 PROMOTION_RULE.md and summarize-timing.py in pins.json before samples, and confirming from the no-op arm's own marks that collectTSAliasRoots is on the fresh no-op path at all. If you send the rebuilt final runtime later I will re-read the two production files and the new test cases on request.
